extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing submissions to The Journal of Symbolic Logic (mathematical logicians)
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Journal of Symbolic Logic
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors preparing research papers for submission to The Journal of Symbolic Logic: expectations about quality, novelty, scope, compliance with author guidelines and ethics, and the decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes research in mathematical logic and its applications of the highest quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are expected to meet the journal's standard of 'highest quality' research. (No quantitative scoring provided on the page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are expected to exhibit innovation and not merely be minor variations on established work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should contribute novel ideas or results rather than small extensions or incremental tweaks of existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should also be of interest to a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work aimed only at a very narrow specialist audience may not meet this expectation; authors should emphasize wider relevance or significance within mathematical logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to author guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for publication, papers should follow the JSL Author Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must consult and comply with the journal's formal author guidelines (formatting, submission procedures, length, bibliographic style, etc.) available via the provided link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication ethics compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should review the ASL’s policy on Publication Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are expected to comply with ethical standards (e.g., originality, authorship, conflicts of interest, plagiarism) as set out by the Association for Symbolic Logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Final decisions to accept papers are made by The Journal editorial board as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is determined by the journal's editorial board; authors should be aware that peer review and board deliberation determine final outcomes.
